records.source: לֵאמֹ֡ר הֵ֣ן יְשַׁלַּ֣ח אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־אִשְׁתּוֹ֩ וְהָלְכָ֨ה מֵאִתּ֜וֹ וְהָיְתָ֣ה לְאִישׁ־אַחֵ֗ר הֲיָשׁ֤וּב אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ ע֔וֹד הֲל֛וֹא חָנ֥וֹף תֶּחֱנַ֖ף הָאָ֣רֶץ הַהִ֑יא וְאַ֗תְּ זָנִית֙ רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים וְשׁ֥וֹב אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהֹוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Saying: if sends away a man his wife, and she goes from him and becomes [wife] to another man, will he return to her again? Not utterly will be polluted the land the that? And you have prostituted [with] companions many; and return to me? declares Yahweh.
pieces: This is the message: If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and marries another man, will he go back to her again? \q Would that land not be thoroughly defiled? \q Yet you have prostituted yourself with many lovers, \q and would you now come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.1: Saying: If a man sends away his wife, and she goes from him and becomes another man's [wife], will he return to her again? \q Would not that land be utterly defiled? \q But you have prostituted yourself with many lovers; \q and would you return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.1: This is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s message: Suppose a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and marries someone else. He cannot take her back again. \q If he did, the whole land would be made unclean. \q My people, you have been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, like a woman with many lovers. \q Do you think you can just come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: saying: the word that usually introduces a message, here standing alone at the head of a new oracle
alternatives: a continuation of the heading at 2:1
"that is to say", tying the verse to chapter 2
decisions.reason: The verse opens with the word that normally follows "The word of the LORD came to me" (as in 2:1), but nothing comes before it here. It may be what is left of such a heading, or it may simply mark what follows as God's message. Either way the words that follow are God's, as "declares the LORD" at the end shows.

decisions.choice: the law of Deuteronomy 24:1-4: a divorced wife who has married another man may not go back to her first husband
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 24:1-4 forbids the first husband to take back a wife he has divorced once she has belonged to another man, and says that doing so would bring sin on the land. Jeremiah asks the question as anyone who knew that law would answer it: no, he will not, and the land would be defiled. Israel stands in the place of the wife, and her case is worse: she has had many lovers.

decisions.choice: prostituted yourself with many lovers: Israel's worship of other gods, pictured as a wife's unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: The covenant between the LORD and Israel is pictured as a marriage, so worshiping other gods is pictured as prostitution and adultery (Exodus 34:15-16; Judges 2:17; Hosea 2:4-7). The "lovers" are the gods Israel turned to, and perhaps also the nations whose help it sought (2:18, 36). The picture is about Israel's worship, not about the conduct of particular women.

decisions.choice: and would you return to me?: a question, spoken as a rebuke
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "and return to me", with the verb in a bare form that can be a question or a command. After the question about the divorced wife, it most likely asks how Israel can think of coming back as if nothing had happened. It can also be read as an invitation, "yet return to me", which the rest of the chapter does make (3:12, 14, 22). The verb "return" (shuv) is the chapter's key word.

decisions.choice: divorces ... marries ... prostituted yourself (B) / been unfaithful (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "sends away" and "becomes another man's"; Balanced and Readable use the ordinary words for divorce and remarriage, as Deuteronomy 24:1-2 does. Readable puts the picture of prostitution as unfaithfulness to God, as Leviticus 20:5-6 and Numbers 15:39 do.

decisions.choice: He cannot take her back again ... My people
decisions.reason: Readable gives the expected answer to the two questions as statements, and says who "you" is: the woman addressed is God's people.

records.heading: Can a divorced wife come back?

records.source: שְׂאִֽי־עֵינַ֨יִךְ עַל־שְׁפָיִ֜ם וּרְאִ֗י אֵיפֹה֙ לֹ֣א שֻׁכַּ֔בְתְּ עַל־דְּרָכִים֙ יָשַׁ֣בְתְּ לָהֶ֔ם כַּעֲרָבִ֖י בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַתַּחֲנִ֣יפִי אֶ֔רֶץ בִּזְנוּתַ֖יִךְ וּבְרָעָתֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Lift your eyes to [the] bare heights and see: where not have you been lain with? By [the] roads you sat for them like an Arab in the wilderness, and you polluted [the] land with your prostitutions and with your wickedness.
pieces: Look up at the bare hilltops and see: \q is there any place where you have not been lain with? \q You sat by the roadsides waiting for lovers, like a nomad in the desert, \q and you have defiled the land with your prostitution and your wickedness.

L.2: Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and see: \q where have you not been lain with? \q By the roads you sat for them like an Arab in the wilderness, \q and you have defiled the land with your prostitution and with your wickedness.

R.2: Look up at the bare hilltops. \q Is there any place where you have not been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q You sat by the roads waiting for lovers, like a desert raider waiting for travelers. \q You have made the land unclean by your unfaithfulness and your evil ways.

decisions.choice: where have you not been lain with: the reading the Hebrew tradition gives for this word
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell a coarser verb for sexual intercourse; the tradition of reading the text aloud replaces it with the plainer "been lain with". It does the same in Deuteronomy 28:30, Isaiah 13:16 and Zechariah 14:2. The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: bare heights: open hilltops where other gods were worshiped
decisions.reason: The word means bare, treeless heights. Hilltops were favorite places for shrines to other gods (2:20; 3:6), so the hills Israel is told to look at are the evidence against her. The same heights return in 3:21, now full of weeping.

decisions.choice: an Arab in the wilderness: a desert dweller who waits by the roads for travelers
decisions.reason: The word names a man of the desert tribes. The picture is of someone sitting by the road watching for passers-by, whether to trade with them or to rob them. Israel sat waiting for lovers just as eagerly (compare Genesis 38:14, where Tamar sits by the road).

decisions.choice: waiting for lovers ... nomad (B) / desert raider waiting for travelers (R)
decisions.reason: "Them" in the Hebrew are the lovers of 3:1, so Balanced and Readable name them. Balanced says "nomad" and Readable "desert raider" for the desert dweller, since "Arab" today calls up a modern people (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: been unfaithful to me ... unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: Readable states plainly what the picture of prostitution means: unfaithfulness to God. It keeps the reader from taking the verse as a story about one woman.

records.source: וַיִּמָּנְע֣וּ רְבִבִ֔ים וּמַלְק֖וֹשׁ ל֣וֹא הָיָ֑ה וּמֵ֨צַח אִשָּׁ֤ה זוֹנָה֙ הָ֣יָה לָ֔ךְ מֵאַ֖נְתְּ הִכָּלֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And were withheld showers, and spring rain not has been; and [the] forehead of a woman [who is] a prostitute was to you; you refused to be ashamed.
pieces: So the showers have been held back, \q and the spring rain has not come. \q Yet your face is as brazen as a prostitute's; \q you will not let yourself feel shame.

L.3: So the showers have been withheld, \q and the spring rain has not come; \q yet you have had the forehead of a prostitute; \q you have refused to be ashamed.

R.3: That is why the showers have stopped \q and the spring rain has not come. \q But you are still as bold as a prostitute. \q You will not feel ashamed.

decisions.choice: showers ... spring rain: the late rains of March and April that fill out the grain before harvest
decisions.reason: Israel's farming depended on the autumn rains that softened the ground and the spring rains that ripened the crops. The covenant warned that unfaithfulness would bring drought (Deuteronomy 11:13-17; 28:23-24). The drought is a sign of the broken covenant, yet Israel still does not see it.

decisions.choice: the forehead of a prostitute: a brazen, shameless face
decisions.reason: The forehead stands for the face a person shows to others. A "hard forehead" is stubborn defiance (Ezekiel 3:7-9). Israel faces God with the bold look of a woman who no longer blushes at what she does.

decisions.choice: as brazen as a prostitute's face (B) / as bold as (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the forehead means, since "forehead" alone does not carry the sense of a shameless face in English (meaning decision m2).

records.source: הֲל֣וֹא מֵעַ֔תָּה קָרָ֥את לִ֖י אָבִ֑י אַלּ֥וּף נְעֻרַ֖י אָֽתָּה׃
records.gloss: Not from now you have called to me: my father, [the] companion of my youth [are] you?
pieces: Have you not just now been calling to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "My father, \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have been my close friend since I was young!

L.4: Have you not just now called to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "My father! \q The companion of my youth [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!

R.4: Even now you call out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "My father! \q You have been my friend since I was young!

decisions.choice: have you not just now called: a reproach for words spoken in a time of trouble
alternatives: will you not from now on call to me ...?
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "yes". In the drought (3:3) the people call out to God with warm words, as if all were well between them; 3:5 shows that their deeds say otherwise. Some read "from now on" as a call to speak this way in future, but the following verse points to words already spoken.

decisions.choice: my father, the companion of my youth: the language of a daughter and of a young wife
decisions.reason: "Companion of her youth" is said of a husband in Proverbs 2:17, and the picture of the marriage continues from 3:1. "My father" looks ahead to 3:19, where God says he longed to be called this, and back to 2:27, where the people say "my father" to a piece of wood.

decisions.choice: the people's words run on into the next verse
decisions.reason: The quotation does not end with this verse: the two questions at the start of 3:5 are also the people's words.

decisions.choice: Even now you call out to me
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question that expects "yes" into a statement, which is what it means.

records.source: הֲיִנְטֹ֣ר לְעוֹלָ֔ם אִם־יִשְׁמֹ֖ר לָנֶ֑צַח הִנֵּ֥ה דִבַּ֛רְתְּוַתַּעֲשִׂ֥י הָרָע֖וֹת וַתּוּכָֽל׃פ
records.gloss: Will he keep [anger] forever, or will he guard [it] to [the] end? Look, you have spoken, and you have done the evil [things], and you have been able.
pieces: Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stay angry forever? \q Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hold on to it to the end?" \q That is how you talk, but you do every evil thing you can.

L.5: Will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keep [anger] forever, \q or will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guard [it] to the end?" \q Look, you have spoken [so], but you have done evil things, and you have been able.

R.5: You will not stay angry forever, will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}? \q You will not be angry to the end!" \q That is what you say. But you keep doing every evil thing you can.

decisions.choice: will he keep anger forever: words that echo God's own promise, said lightly
decisions.reason: "Keep" and "guard" are used of holding on to anger (Leviticus 19:18; Nahum 1:2), and Psalm 103:9 says of God that he will not keep his anger forever. The people use that truth as an excuse while they go on sinning. God answers the same words in 3:12: "I will not keep anger forever", but only after they acknowledge their guilt (3:13).

decisions.choice: you have done evil things, and you have been able: you did all the evil you could
decisions.reason: The last verb means "you were able, you prevailed". Joined to "you have done evil things", it says that they did evil to the full, as far as they could, while saying pious words.

decisions.choice: you have spoken: an older spelling of the form for a woman addressed
decisions.reason: The written consonants have an ending that looks like "I have spoken"; it is an older spelling of "you have spoken" (said to a woman), and the reading tradition gives the usual form. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: You will not stay angry forever, will you?
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the people speaking to God directly, as in 3:4, and turns the questions into the hopeful statements they are. In the Hebrew they speak of God as "he".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י בִּימֵי֙ יֹאשִׁיָּ֣הוּ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ הֲֽרָאִ֔יתָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשְׂתָ֖ה מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֹלְכָ֨ה הִ֜יא עַל־כָּל־הַ֣ר גָּבֹ֗הַּ וְאֶל־תַּ֛חַת כָּל־עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָ֖ן וַתִּזְנִי־שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me in [the] days of Josiah the king: Have you seen what has done faithless Israel? Going she [was] onto every hill high and to under every tree green, and she prostituted there.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to me during the reign of King Josiah: "Have you seen what faithless Israel did? She went up onto every high hill and under every green tree, and there she prostituted herself.

L.6: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me in the days of Josiah the king, "Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She has been going up onto every high hill and under every green tree, and she has prostituted herself there.

R.6: When Josiah was king, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} asked me, "Did you see what faithless Israel did? She went up to every high hill and under every green tree to worship other gods. She was unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} there.

decisions.choice: the days of Josiah: king of Judah from about 640 to 609 BC
decisions.reason: Jeremiah began to prophesy in Josiah's thirteenth year (1:2). The northern kingdom of Israel had fallen to Assyria about a century before (2 Kings 17), and Josiah later led a reform in Judah (2 Kings 22-23). This prose section (3:6-18) speaks of the two kingdoms as two sisters.

decisions.choice: faithless Israel: Israel named for her turning away
decisions.reason: The word is a noun, "turning away" or "apostasy", used here as a name: "Turning-Away Israel". It comes from the verb shuv, "turn, return", the key word of the chapter, so the name says that Israel's whole character is to turn from God. In 3:12 God calls her by this name and tells her to turn back.

decisions.choice: every high hill and under every green tree: the places of worship of other gods
decisions.reason: The phrase is the standard description of the shrines of other gods in the hills and groves (Deuteronomy 12:2; 2 Kings 17:10; Jeremiah 2:20). Israel's "prostitution" there is the worship of those gods.

decisions.choice: faithless
decisions.reason: The name is put as an adjective, "faithless", at every level, so that it matches "faithless children" in 3:14 and 3:22, which come from the same verb. "Backsliding" is older church language and "apostate" is not an everyday word.

decisions.choice: to worship other gods. She was unfaithful to me there
decisions.reason: Readable says what Israel did on the hills, which the picture of prostitution means (meaning decision m3).

records.heading: Faithless Israel and treacherous Judah

records.source: וָאֹמַ֗ר אַחֲרֵ֨י עֲשׂוֹתָ֧הּ אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֛לֶּה אֵלַ֥י תָּשׁ֖וּב וְלֹא־שָׁ֑בָה וַתֵּ֛רֶא בָּגוֹדָ֥ה אֲחוֹתָ֖הּ יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And I said: after her doing all these, to me she will return; and not she returned; and saw [it] her treacherous sister Judah.
pieces: I thought, 'After she has done all this, she will come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.' But she did not come back, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

L.7: And I said, 'After she has done all these [things], she will return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.' But she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw [it].

R.7: I thought, 'After she has done all this, she will come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.' But she did not come back. And her sister Judah, who also betrayed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, saw it all.

decisions.choice: treacherous: one who breaks faith, especially in marriage
decisions.reason: The word describes someone who betrays a trust, and it is used of an unfaithful spouse (Malachi 2:14-16; Jeremiah 3:20). Israel is "faithless", named for turning away; Judah is "treacherous", named for betraying.

decisions.choice: and she saw: the reading tradition's form of the verb
decisions.reason: The written consonants spell the verb with an extra letter; the reading tradition gives the ordinary form "and she saw". The sense is not affected.

decisions.choice: who also betrayed me
decisions.reason: Readable explains "treacherous" in plain words.

records.source: וָאֵ֗רֶא כִּ֤י עַל־כָּל־אֹדוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נִֽאֲפָה֙ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל שִׁלַּחְתִּ֕יהָ וָאֶתֵּ֛ן אֶת־סֵ֥פֶר כְּרִיתֻתֶ֖יהָ אֵלֶ֑יהָ וְלֹ֨א יָֽרְאָ֜ה בֹּֽגֵדָ֤ה יְהוּדָה֙ אֲחוֹתָ֔הּ וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ וַתִּ֥זֶן גַּם־הִֽיא׃
records.gloss: And I saw that, for all [the] causes that committed adultery faithless Israel, I sent her away and gave [the] document of her divorce to her; and not feared treacherous Judah her sister, and she went and prostituted, also she.
pieces: I saw that, because faithless Israel had committed adultery, I sent her away and gave her a certificate of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid. She too went and prostituted herself.

L.8: And I saw that, for all the reasons that faithless Israel committed adultery, I sent her away and gave her the certificate of her divorce; yet her treacherous sister Judah was not afraid, but she too went and prostituted herself.

R.8: Faithless Israel was unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in many ways. So I sent her away and gave her divorce papers. I saw that her sister, treacherous Judah, was not afraid even then. She went and was unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} too.

decisions.choice: I sent her away and gave her the certificate of her divorce: the steps of Deuteronomy 24:1
decisions.reason: God's dealing with northern Israel is described in the words of the divorce law Jeremiah raised in 3:1. The "divorce" is the kingdom's destruction and the exile of its people by Assyria in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:6-23). Isaiah 50:1 uses the same picture.

decisions.choice: and I saw: the Hebrew has God as the one who saw
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "I saw". A few ancient translations, such as the Syriac, read "and she saw", making Judah the one who saw what happened to Israel, as in 3:7. The Hebrew makes sense as it stands: God saw that Judah was not afraid.

decisions.choice: committed adultery: broke the marriage covenant by worshiping other gods
decisions.reason: The marriage picture continues: the adultery is Israel's worship of other gods (3:9).

decisions.choice: because faithless Israel had committed adultery (B) / unfaithful to me in many ways (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "for all the reasons that" is put as "because" at Balanced. Readable lets "all" become "in many ways" and puts the events in order, then "I saw".

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ מִקֹּ֣ל זְנוּתָ֔הּ וַתֶּחֱנַ֖ף אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַתִּנְאַ֥ף אֶת־הָאֶ֖בֶן וְאֶת־הָעֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: And it was, from [the] lightness of her prostitution, and she polluted the land; and she committed adultery with the stone and with the wood.
pieces: Because her prostitution meant so little to her, she defiled the land, committing adultery with stone and wood.

L.9: And because her prostitution [was] a light [thing to her], she defiled the land, and she committed adultery with stone and with wood.

R.9: She did not take her unfaithfulness seriously. She made the land unclean and worshiped idols of stone and wood, which was like committing adultery.

decisions.choice: the lightness of her prostitution: she treated it as a small thing
decisions.reason: The noun means lightness, the opposite of weight or seriousness. Her unfaithfulness meant little to her. Some read a related word, "noise" or "report", but "lightness" fits the charge.

decisions.choice: she defiled the land: the verb with an object
decisions.reason: This verb usually means "be defiled", but here it has an object, "the land", so the sense is that she defiled it (compare 3:1-2). Who "she" is is left open: the verse may still speak of Israel, whose story 3:6-8 tells, or of Judah, named last. The verse holds for both.

decisions.choice: stone and wood: idols and sacred objects of the other gods
decisions.reason: Standing stones and wooden poles or images stood at the shrines of other gods (Deuteronomy 16:21-22). Jeremiah mocks the people for calling a piece of wood "my father" and a stone "you gave me birth" (2:27).

decisions.choice: worshiped idols of stone and wood, which was like committing adultery
decisions.reason: Readable says what the adultery with stone and wood was, the worship of idols (meaning decision m3), and keeps the picture as a comparison.

records.source: וְגַם־בְּכָל־זֹ֗את לֹא־שָׁ֨בָה אֵלַ֜י בָּגוֹדָ֧ה אֲחוֹתָ֛הּ יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּכָל־לִבָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י אִם־בְּשֶׁ֖קֶר נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And also in all this not returned to me her treacherous sister Judah with all her heart, but only in falsehood, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Even after all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} wholeheartedly; it was only a pretense, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.10: And even so, for all this, her treacherous sister Judah did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with all her heart, but only in pretense, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.10: Even after all this, her sister, treacherous Judah, did not truly come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. She only pretended to, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: in falsehood: a return that was only outward
decisions.reason: The word means a lie or a deception. Judah made a show of turning back to God, but her heart was not in it. In the setting of Josiah's days (3:6) this may point to the people's response to his reform (2 Kings 22-23), which did not change their hearts; the verse itself does not say so.

decisions.choice: with all her heart: the return God asks for
decisions.reason: To return "with all the heart" is the language of Deuteronomy for real repentance (Deuteronomy 4:29; 30:10). God measures the return by the heart, not by outward signs. The same words are said of Josiah himself in 2 Kings 23:25.

decisions.choice: did not truly come back ... She only pretended to
decisions.reason: Readable puts "with all her heart" as "truly" and "in falsehood" as pretending.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י צִדְּקָ֥ה נַפְשָׁ֖הּ מְשֻׁבָ֣ה יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מִבֹּגֵדָ֖ה יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me: has shown righteous her soul faithless Israel more than treacherous Judah.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself less guilty than treacherous Judah.

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

R.11: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Faithless Israel was not as guilty as treacherous Judah.

decisions.choice: has shown herself more righteous than: is less in the wrong than
decisions.reason: The verb means "be in the right" and, in this form, "show to be in the right". Set beside Judah, Israel comes out better: not innocent, but less guilty. Judah had Israel's fall before her eyes and still did not turn back (3:7-10). Ezekiel 16:51-52 makes the same comparison, and Genesis 38:26 uses the same kind of saying ("she is more in the right than I").

decisions.choice: herself: literally "her soul"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "her soul" (nefesh), which here, as often, stands for the person herself.

decisions.choice: less guilty
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "less guilty" so that no reader takes "more righteous" as praise of Israel (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the Hebrew's "more righteous".

records.heading: Return, faithless people

records.source: הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֨ים הָאֵ֜לֶּה צָפ֗וֹנָה וְ֠אָמַרְתָּ שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לֽוֹא־אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־חָסִ֤יד אֲנִי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לֹ֥א אֶטּ֖וֹר לְעוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: Go and proclaim these words toward [the] north and say: return, faithless Israel, declares Yahweh; not I will make fall my face on you, for loyal [am] I, declares Yahweh; not I will keep [anger] forever.
pieces: Go and proclaim this message toward the north: 'Return, faithless Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will not look on you in anger, for I am loyal in love, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will not stay angry forever.

L.12: Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, 'Return, faithless Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I will not make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face fall on you, for I [am] loyal, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; I will not keep [anger] forever.

R.12: Go and announce this message toward the north, where the people of Israel were taken: 'Come back, faithless Israel, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will not look at you in anger. My love is faithful, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will not stay angry forever.

decisions.choice: return, faithless Israel: a play on words, "turn back, Turning-Away Israel"
decisions.reason: The command and the name come from the same verb, shuv: "Return, Turning-Away". The one whose name is turning away is called to turn back, and the play runs through the chapter (3:1, 7, 10, 14, 22; 4:1). The name is explained at 3:6.

decisions.choice: toward the north: toward the lands where northern Israel had been taken in exile
decisions.reason: Assyria had deported the people of the northern kingdom to the north and east (2 Kings 17:6). The message is sent to them, though they are far away.

decisions.choice: I will not make my face fall on you: I will not look on you in anger
decisions.reason: A fallen face is an angry or displeased face (Genesis 4:5-6). God promises not to turn a hostile look on his people.

decisions.choice: loyal: one who keeps faith and shows loyal love
decisions.reason: The word is related to hesed, the loyal love that keeps a covenant. God's reason for not keeping his anger is his own character. It answers the people's careless question in 3:5 with the same verb, "keep".

decisions.choice: the message to proclaim runs on through 3:18
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not mark where the words Jeremiah is to proclaim end. They are taken here to run to the end of 3:18, since 3:13-18 go on speaking to the same people about their return.

decisions.choice: loyal in love (B) / My love is faithful (R)
decisions.reason: The word is put as "loyal in love" at Balanced and as faithful love at Readable, matching the wording for hesed (meaning decision m4). "Return, faithless Israel" cannot keep the Hebrew pun (meaning decision m1); "faithless" gives the sense of the name, as in 3:6.

decisions.choice: where the people of Israel were taken
decisions.reason: Readable says why the message goes north (meaning decision m2).

records.source: אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ כִּ֛י בַּיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהַ֖יִךְ פָּשָׁ֑עַתְּ וַתְּפַזְּרִ֨י אֶת־דְּרָכַ֜יִךְ לַזָּרִ֗ים תַּ֚חַת כָּל־עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֔ן וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא־שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהֹוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Only know your iniquity, that against Yahweh your God you rebelled, and you scattered your ways to strangers under every tree green, and to my voice not you listened, declares Yahweh.
pieces: Only admit your guilt: you have rebelled against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, you have run here and there to foreign gods under every green tree, and you have not obeyed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.13: Only acknowledge your iniquity, that you have rebelled against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and have scattered your ways to strangers under every green tree, and you have not listened to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} voice, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.13: Just admit that you have sinned. You turned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You gave yourself to foreign gods under every green tree. You did not obey {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: acknowledge: know and admit
decisions.reason: "Know" here means to recognize one's guilt and own it. This is the one condition God sets for the return he offers: not ceremonies, but honest admission.

decisions.choice: scattered your ways to strangers: went this way and that after foreign gods
decisions.reason: To "scatter your ways" is to run off in many directions. The "strangers" are foreign gods, the lovers of 3:1-2, as in 2:25 ("I have loved strangers").

decisions.choice: you have not listened: the address changes from one woman to many people
decisions.reason: Until here "you" is one woman, Israel. The last verb is plural, and from 3:14 God speaks to the people as a group.

decisions.choice: run here and there to foreign gods (B) / gave yourself to foreign gods (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom and name the strangers as foreign gods (meaning decision m2).

records.source: שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י בָּעַ֣לְתִּי בָכֶ֑ם וְלָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֜ם אֶחָ֣ד מֵעִ֗יר וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ מִמִּשְׁפָּחָ֔ה וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם צִיּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Return, faithless sons, declares Yahweh, for I, I am husband over you; and I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and I will bring you [to] Zion.
pieces: Return, faithless {{gender:children|sons}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for I am your husband. I will take you, one from a town and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.

L.14: Return, faithless {{gender:children|sons}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for I am husband to you; and I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and I will bring you to Zion.

R.14: Come back, faithless {{gender:children|sons}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as a wife belongs to her husband. I will take you, one from a town and two from a family, and bring you to Zion.

decisions.choice: faithless children: children who have turned away
decisions.reason: The adjective comes from the same verb as "return", so "Return, faithless children" is a play on words like 3:12: "Turn back, you who have turned away". The picture moves from a wife to children, and "children" means the whole people.

decisions.choice: I am husband to you: I am your husband and lord
decisions.reason: The verb means to be a husband, and also to be master or lord. It is the verb from which the name Baal ("lord, owner") comes, so it may also say that the LORD, not Baal, is Israel's true lord. The marriage picture of 3:1-11 makes "husband" the main sense; Jeremiah 31:32 uses the verb the same way.

decisions.choice: one from a town and two from a clan: a few, gathered one by one
decisions.reason: The numbers are small on purpose. God will not wait for the whole nation; he will bring back even scattered individuals. A clan was the group of related families within a tribe.

decisions.choice: you belong to me as a wife belongs to her husband
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the marriage picture behind the verb (meaning decision m2).

records.source: וְנָתַתִּ֥י לָכֶ֛ם רֹעִ֖ים כְּלִבִּ֑י וְרָע֥וּ אֶתְכֶ֖ם דֵּעָ֥ה וְהַשְׂכֵּֽיל׃
records.gloss: And I will give to you shepherds according to my heart, and they will shepherd you [with] knowledge and insight.
pieces: I will give you shepherds who are after {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge and insight.

L.15: And I will give you shepherds according to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart, and they will shepherd you [with] knowledge and insight.

R.15: I will give you leaders who will care for you as I want them to. They will lead you with knowledge and wisdom.

decisions.choice: shepherds: kings and leaders of the people
decisions.reason: In Jeremiah, "shepherds" are the people's rulers (2:8; 23:1-4). Those who led Israel astray will be replaced by rulers who do God's will.

decisions.choice: according to my heart: chosen by God and doing what he wants
decisions.reason: God said the same of the king he would choose in Saul's place, David (1 Samuel 13:14), and of the faithful priest (1 Samuel 2:35). Jeremiah 23:4-5 promises such shepherds and a king from David's line.

decisions.choice: leaders who will care for you ... lead you
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of shepherds as leaders who care for the people, and "after my heart" as acting as God wants.

records.source: וְהָיָ֡ה כִּ֣י תִרְבּוּ֩ וּפְרִיתֶ֨ם בָּאָ֜רֶץ בַּיָּמִ֤ים הָהֵ֨מָּה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לֹא־יֹ֣אמְרוּ ע֗וֹד אֲרוֹן֙ בְּרִית־יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־לֵ֑ב וְלֹ֤א יִזְכְּרוּ־בוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א יִפְקֹ֔דוּ וְלֹ֥א יֵעָשֶׂ֖ה עֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when you multiply and are fruitful in the land in the days the those, declares Yahweh, not they will say again: [the] ark of [the] covenant of Yahweh; and not it will come up on [the] heart, and not they will remember it, and not they will miss [it], and not it will be made again.
pieces: In those days, when you have multiplied and been fruitful in the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, people will no longer speak of "the ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." It will not come to mind; they will not remember it or miss it, and another will not be made.

L.16: And it will be, when you multiply and are fruitful in the land in those days, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they will no longer say, "The ark of the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}," and it will not come up on [the] heart, and they will not remember it, and they will not miss [it], and it will not be made again.

R.16: In those days there will be many of you in the land, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Then people will no longer talk about the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant. They will not think about it or remember it. They will not miss it, and no one will make another one.

decisions.choice: the ark no longer remembered: God's presence will no longer be tied to the ark
decisions.reason: The ark of the covenant was the chest that held the covenant tablets, and it was the place where God was enthroned among his people (1 Samuel 4:4; Psalm 99:1). The promise is not that God will be forgotten, but that the ark will no longer be needed: in 3:17 the whole of Jerusalem is called the LORD's throne. The text does not say what became of the ark; it is not among the temple treasures taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:13-17).

decisions.choice: multiply and are fruitful: the blessing of Genesis restored
decisions.reason: The two verbs recall God's blessing at creation and to the ancestors (Genesis 1:28; 35:11), here in reverse order. The people who return will grow in number in the land again.

decisions.choice: miss it: feel its absence
decisions.reason: The verb means to look for something and notice it is gone. No one will feel the ark is missing.

decisions.choice: come to mind (B) / think about it (R)
decisions.reason: "Come up on the heart" is a Hebrew way of saying that something comes to mind; Literal keeps the picture.

records.source: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא יִקְרְא֤וּ לִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ כִּסֵּ֣א יְהוָ֔ה וְנִקְוּ֨וּ אֵלֶ֧יהָ כָֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֛ם לְשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה לִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא־יֵלְכ֣וּ ע֔וֹד אַחֲרֵ֕י שְׁרִר֖וּת לִבָּ֥ם הָרָֽע׃ס
records.gloss: At the time the that they will call Jerusalem [the] throne of Yahweh, and will be gathered to it all the nations, to [the] name of Yahweh, to Jerusalem; and not they will walk again after [the] stubbornness of their heart the evil.
pieces: At that time Jerusalem will be named {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s throne, and all the nations will gather in Jerusalem to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s name. No longer will they follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.

L.17: At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and all the nations will be gathered to it, to the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to Jerusalem; and they will no longer walk after the stubbornness of their evil heart.

R.17: At that time people will call Jerusalem {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s throne. All the nations will come together there to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Jerusalem. They will no longer stubbornly follow their own evil hearts.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem the throne of the LORD: the whole city as the place of God's rule
decisions.reason: What the ark once was, the place of God's throne among his people (3:16), the whole city will be. Jeremiah 14:21 and 17:12 also speak of God's throne in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: all the nations gathered to the name of the LORD: the nations come to worship
decisions.reason: The "name" of the LORD stands for his presence and honor. The picture of the nations streaming to Jerusalem is shared with Isaiah 2:2-4 and 60:3.

decisions.choice: they will no longer walk: most naturally the nations, who also turn from their stubbornness
decisions.reason: The nearest subject is "all the nations". The phrase about the stubbornness of an evil heart is used elsewhere in Jeremiah of Israel and Judah (7:24; 9:13), so it may also include God's own people.

decisions.choice: to honor (B) / to worship (R)
decisions.reason: "To the name of the LORD" is put as coming to honor or worship him (meaning decision m2).

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔מָּה יֵלְכ֥וּ בֵית־יְהוּדָ֖ה עַל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְיָבֹ֤אוּ יַחְדָּו֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן עַל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִנְחַ֖לְתִּי אֶת־אֲבוֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: In the days the those will walk [the] house of Judah with [the] house of Israel, and they will come together from [the] land of [the] north to the land that I gave as inheritance [to] your fathers.
pieces: In those days the people of Judah will join the people of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} as their inheritance.'"

L.18: In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land that I gave as an inheritance to your fathers.'"

R.18: In those days the people of Judah and the people of Israel will join together. They will come together from the land in the north to the land I gave your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} to be their own.'"

decisions.choice: the house of Judah with the house of Israel: the two kingdoms reunited
decisions.reason: The sisters of 3:6-11, divided since Solomon's death (1 Kings 12), will return as one people. Ezekiel 37:15-22 and Hosea 2:2 give the same hope. The verse looks ahead to an exile of Judah too, since Judah also comes back "from the land of the north".

decisions.choice: the land of the north: the lands of exile
decisions.reason: Invaders from Assyria and Babylon reached Israel from the north, so "the north" stands for the lands of exile (3:12; 16:15; 23:8).

decisions.choice: the people of Judah ... the people of Israel
decisions.reason: "House" here means the whole people descended from one ancestor, so Balanced and Readable say "people".

records.source: וְאָנֹכִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֵ֚יךְ אֲשִׁיתֵ֣ךְ בַּבָּנִ֔ים וְאֶתֶּן־לָךְ֙ אֶ֣רֶץ חֶמְדָּ֔ה נַחֲלַ֥ת צְבִ֖י צִבְא֣וֹת גּוֹיִ֑ם וָאֹמַ֗ר אָבִי֙ תִּקְרְאִי־לִ֔י וּמֵאַחֲרַ֖י לֹ֥א תָשֽׁוּבִי׃
records.gloss: And I, I said: how I will set you among the sons and give to you a land of desire, an inheritance of beauty of [the] beauties of nations; and I said: my father you will call me, and from after me not you will turn back.
pieces: I myself thought, "How I would love to treat you as one of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sons \q and give you a pleasant land, \q the most beautiful inheritance among the nations!" \q I thought you would call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} "My father" \q and would never turn away from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

L.19: And I, I said, "How I will set you among the sons \q and give you a desirable land, \q an inheritance, the most beautiful of the nations!" \q And I said, "'My father' you will call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and from following {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} you will not turn back."

R.19: I thought, "I want to treat you like {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own son. \q I want to give you a good land, the most beautiful land of any nation." \q I thought you would call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} "My father" \q and never turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: set you among the sons: give you a son's share of the inheritance
decisions.reason: God speaks to Israel as a daughter ("you" is feminine). In Israel the land passed to sons; daughters inherited only where there were no sons (Numbers 27:1-11). God wanted to treat his daughter as a son and give her the best land of all.

decisions.choice: how I will set you: an exclamation of longing
alternatives: How can I set you among the sons?
decisions.reason: "How" here begins an exclamation of what God gladly planned for his people, not a question. It can also be read as a question, "How can I put you among the sons?", asking how such a thing could be done, which would make the verse a statement of grace that overcomes the obstacle.

decisions.choice: an inheritance, the most beautiful of the nations: the finest land of all
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "a beauty of beauties of the nations", repeating the word to make a superlative. The land is the "beautiful land" of Daniel 8:9 and 11:16.

decisions.choice: you will call ... you will not turn back: said to one woman
decisions.reason: The written consonants have these two verbs in the plural ("you all will call"); the reading tradition gives them as singular, matching the feminine "you" earlier in the verse. The sense is the same: the people as a whole.

decisions.choice: I thought you would call me "My father"
decisions.reason: The second thing God said is put as indirect speech at Balanced and Readable, which reads more naturally and keeps the sense of a hope that was not fulfilled.

decisions.choice: one of my sons (B) / like my own son (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose sons are meant, God's own.

records.source: אָכֵ֛ן בָּגְדָ֥ה אִשָּׁ֖ה מֵרֵעָ֑הּ כֵּ֣ן בְּגַדְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Surely [as] betrays a woman from her companion, so you have betrayed me, house of Israel, declares Yahweh.
pieces: But as an unfaithful wife leaves her husband, \q so you have been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, house of Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.20: But as a woman betrays her companion, \q so you have betrayed {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, house of Israel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.20: But you have been unfaithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, people of Israel, \q like a wife who leaves her husband, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: betrays ... have betrayed: broken faith, as in a marriage
decisions.reason: This is the verb behind "treacherous Judah" in 3:7-11. Here it is said of the whole house of Israel.

decisions.choice: her companion: her husband
decisions.reason: The word means a friend or companion. Beside "a woman" and the picture of 3:1-5, it means her husband, as in Hosea 3:1.

decisions.choice: but: the word marks a contrast with God's hopes in 3:19
decisions.reason: The adverb can mean "surely" or "but in fact". Here it sets what Israel did against what God had hoped.

decisions.choice: unfaithful ... leaves her husband
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the betrayal in the terms of marriage, which the verse compares.

records.source: ק֚וֹל עַל־שְׁפָיִ֣ים נִשְׁמָ֔ע בְּכִ֥י תַחֲנוּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י הֶעֱוּוּ֙ אֶת־דַּרְכָּ֔ם שָׁכְח֖וּ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: A voice on [the] bare heights is heard, [the] weeping of [the] pleading of [the] sons of Israel; for they have perverted their way, they have forgotten Yahweh their God.
pieces: A cry is heard on the bare hilltops, \q the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} weeping and pleading, \q because they have twisted their path \q and forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

L.21: A sound is heard on the bare heights, \q the weeping [and] pleading of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, \q for they have perverted their way; \q they have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

R.21: A sound comes from the bare hilltops. \q The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} are crying and begging for mercy. \q They have gone the wrong way. \q They have forgotten {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: the bare heights: the hilltops of 3:2
decisions.reason: The heights where Israel worshiped other gods (3:2) are now the place where its people weep. The weeping may be for the drought (3:3) or a lament before the gods of the hills; the next verse shows God answering it with a call to return.

decisions.choice: pleading: prayers asking for mercy
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "show favor" and means pleas for mercy.

decisions.choice: perverted their way: made their path crooked
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend or twist. Israel's "way", its manner of life, has become crooked.

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: "The sons of Israel" means the whole people, men and women, so the gender setting applies.

records.source: שׁ֚וּבוּ בָּנִ֣ים שׁוֹבָבִ֔ים אֶרְפָּ֖ה מְשׁוּבֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם הִנְנוּ֙ אָתָ֣נוּ לָ֔ךְ כִּ֥י אַתָּ֖ה יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Return, faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness. Here we [are]; we have come to you, for you [are] Yahweh our God.
pieces: Return, faithless {{gender:children|sons}}, \q and I will heal your faithlessness. \q "We are here; we have come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

L.22: Return, faithless {{gender:children|sons}}; \q I will heal your faithlessness. \q "Here we [are]; we have come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

R.22: Come back, faithless {{gender:children|sons}}. \q I will heal you of your unfaithfulness. \q "Yes, we are coming to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God.

decisions.choice: Return ... I will heal your faithlessness: God's call of 3:14 with a promise
decisions.reason: The call repeats 3:14, and the play on "return" continues: "Turn back, you who have turned away; I will heal your turnings away." Hosea 14:5 promises the same: "I will heal their faithlessness." Faithlessness is pictured as a sickness only God can heal.

decisions.choice: Here we are; we have come to you: the people answer
decisions.reason: The speaker changes without warning: the people reply to God's call. Their words run on to the end of 3:25. They are set in quotation marks to show the new voice.

decisions.choice: heal you of your unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that it is the people who are healed of their unfaithfulness.

records.source: אָכֵ֥ן לַשֶּׁ֛קֶר מִגְּבָע֖וֹת הָמ֣וֹן הָרִ֑ים אָכֵן֙ בַּיהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ תְּשׁוּעַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: Surely for deception from [the] hills, [the] tumult [of the] mountains; surely in Yahweh our God [is] the salvation of Israel.
pieces: Surely the hills are a delusion, and the uproar on the mountains; \q surely in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God \q is the salvation of Israel.

L.23: Surely [it is] for deception, from the hills, the tumult [on] the mountains; \q surely in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God \q [is] the salvation of Israel.

R.23: The noisy worship on the hills and mountains was a lie. \q It is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God who truly saves Israel.

decisions.choice: the hills ... the tumult on the mountains: the noisy worship at the hill shrines was a deception
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very compressed: "surely for deception from the hills, the tumult of the mountains". It most likely means that the crowds and noise of the festivals for other gods on the hills (3:2, 6) promised help but gave none. The word for tumult can also mean wealth, which would make the line say that what came from the hills was a fraud.

decisions.choice: in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel: help is found in him alone
decisions.reason: The repeated "surely" sets the two halves against each other: the hills deceive; the LORD saves. This is what God asked for in 3:13: an honest acknowledgment.

decisions.choice: The noisy worship ... It is the LORD our God who truly saves
decisions.reason: Readable explains the tumult as noisy worship and puts "surely" as "truly".

records.source: וְהַבֹּ֗שֶׁת אָֽכְלָ֛ה אֶת־יְגִ֥יעַ אֲבוֹתֵ֖ינוּ מִנְּעוּרֵ֑ינוּ אֶת־צֹאנָם֙ וְאֶת־בְּקָרָ֔ם אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־בְּנוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And the shame has devoured [the] toil of our fathers from our youth, their flock and their herd, their sons and their daughters.
pieces: From our youth the shameful god has devoured all that our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} worked for: \q their flocks and their herds, \q their sons and their daughters.

L.24: And the shameful thing has devoured the toil of our fathers from our youth: \q their flocks and their herds, \q their sons and their daughters.

R.24: Ever since we were young, the shameful god Baal has eaten up everything our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} worked for. \q It took their flocks and herds, and even their sons and daughters.

decisions.choice: the shameful thing: a scornful name for Baal
decisions.reason: "Shame" is used in place of the name Baal (Jeremiah 11:13; Hosea 9:10), as in names where "bosheth" replaces "baal" (Ishbosheth, 2 Samuel 2:8, also called Eshbaal in 1 Chronicles 8:33). The people now call their god what he was.

decisions.choice: devoured flocks, herds, sons and daughters: offerings to Baal
decisions.reason: The worship of Baal took the animals offered to him and, at its worst, children sacrificed in fire (Jeremiah 19:5; 2 Kings 17:17). The confession counts everything it cost.

decisions.choice: the shameful god Baal
decisions.reason: Readable names the god behind the scornful title (meaning decision m1).

records.source: נִשְׁכְּבָ֣ה בְּבָשְׁתֵּ֗נוּ וּֽתְכַסֵּנוּ֮ כְּלִמָּתֵנוּ֒ כִּי֩ לַיהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ חָטָ֗אנוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ֙ וַאֲבוֹתֵ֔ינוּ מִנְּעוּרֵ֖ינוּ וְעַד־הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֣א שָׁמַ֔עְנוּ בְּק֖וֹל יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃ס
records.gloss: Let us lie down in our shame, and let cover us our disgrace, for against Yahweh our God we have sinned, we and our fathers, from our youth and until the day the this, and not we have listened to [the] voice of Yahweh our God.
pieces: Let us lie down in our shame and let our disgrace cover us. \q For both we and our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, \q from our youth until this very day, \q and we have not obeyed the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."

L.25: Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us, \q for we have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, we and our fathers, \q from our youth and until this day, \q and we have not listened to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."

R.25: Let us lie down in our shame, covered by our disgrace. \q We and our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God \q from the time we were young until today. \q We have not obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God."

decisions.choice: let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us: a full admission of guilt
decisions.reason: The people picture themselves lying down with shame as their bed and disgrace as their covering. They no longer refuse to be ashamed (3:3); they make the acknowledgment God asked for (3:13).

decisions.choice: we and our fathers ... we have not listened: guilt shared across generations
decisions.reason: The confession owns the sin of the past generations as well as their own (compare Psalm 106:6; Daniel 9:8). It ends where 3:13 ended: they have not listened to God's voice.

decisions.choice: obeyed
decisions.reason: "Listen to the voice of" means to obey, so Balanced and Readable say "obey", as in 3:13.
